title: fix(scripts): the objectui changeset digest reads a BREAKING annotation behind a warning sign
body:
Fixes #23112

Clause-②: no

## What changed

One file, `scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs`:

- **`BREAKING_BLOCK_OPENER`** now admits a decoration between the heading or bullet mark and the word. A decoration is a run of pictographic symbols (Unicode `Extended_Pictographic`), each with an optional variation selector (U+FE0E / U+FE0F). It can sit on either side of the emphasis mark: `## ⚠️ BREAKING`, `⚠️ **BREAKING`, `**⚠️ Breaking`. The rule is still anchored at the line start. It admits no letter, no digit and no ASCII punctuation, so it is not a "contains BREAKING anywhere" match. On a line with no pictograph, the new fragment can only match the empty string, so the rule behaves exactly as it did before.
- **`OPENS_WITH_BREAKING_LABEL`** admits the same decoration. This is the test `markBreaking` uses so that an author's own label is not stamped a second time. Without this change, the opener fix would make the digest print a doubled marker; details under *Bounded in-place fix* below.
- **Self-test:** a new battery, `#23112: a DECORATED annotation — a pictograph before the word`, with 16 cases and a floor of 16. The roster floor goes from 16 to 17.

## Corpus reading: which decorations occur, and does the rule raise a false positive

**Tree:** a blobless clone of `objectstack-ai/objectui` covering every head (4121 refs, `main` at `5595aabca30b`). Every blob ever written under `.changeset/*.md` (README excluded) was then fetched in full: 5678 blobs over 4810 paths. Each body was parsed with the digest's own `parseChangeset` and walked with `hasBreakingAnnotation`'s own block-start logic. 704 block-head lines carry the word.

**Distinct decorations in front of the word (after the heading or bullet mark):** exactly one, U+26A0 WARNING SIGN + U+FE0F (`⚠️`), in four placements:

| placement | blobs | paths |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `## ⚠️ BREAKING …` (heading) | 18 | 14 |
| `⚠️ **BREAKING …` (before the emphasis mark) | 22 | 11 |
| `⚠️ Breaking …` (plain paragraph) | 8 | 7 |
| `**⚠️ Breaking …` (inside the emphasis mark) | 3 | 1 |
| **union** | **51** | **33** |

- **Base rule (`21c86444e`):** 47 of those 51 blobs (30 paths) read as **not breaking**. The other 4 were caught by an unrelated signal.
- **This rule:** 0 missed.

**False positives, over the same corpus:**

- **Prose lines:** a block-head line whose text before the word contains a letter or digit is prose (144 blobs / 108 paths). The new rule admits **0** of them.
- **Lost readings:** blobs the base rule reads as breaking and this rule does not: **0**.
- **Newly admitted lines:** 16 distinct texts, and each one is a decorated declaration. Examples: `## ⚠️ BREAKING for a host that hands reference_to to the widgets directly`, `⚠️ **BREAKING if your code hands a numeric primary key to any of these three:**`, `⚠️ Breaking change (marked minor under this repo's version policy): the …`.
- **Doubled markers** in rendered summaries (`**BREAKING** — ⚠️ **BREAKING …`): 0 with this change. If only the opener were fixed, there would be 4 blobs / 2 paths (`10719-retire-phase35-validation-types.md`, `7659-retire-validation-engine.md`).

**Why a pictograph class rather than either option the card names:**

- **Not "any non-word, non-space run":** ASCII punctuation in front of the word is a prose shape in this same corpus. Counts: `(` 39 blobs (`(breaking, declared minor per the version policy)`), `—` 5, `"` 2 (`described under "Breaking for TypeScript readers" below`), `("` 1, `(**` 1. A code span such as a backticked identifier named breaking would also count. Admitting any of these trades the miss for false positives.
- **Not an enumerated `⚠️`:** that fixes the corpus, but the next author's `🚨 BREAKING` would be the same miss again.
- **The pictograph class:** it admits no ASCII and no letter, and it shows zero false positives on the corpus.

## The hop range `7578323a544e..1fb1ced36243`

Before (base `21c86444e`):

```text
→ 10 releasing changeset(s), 1 breaking (0 declared major, 1 annotated), 1 release-nothing, 2 commit(s) without a changeset
⚠️ 1 of these carries a breaking change: 1 by the author's own breaking annotation in the changeset body — …
```

After (`ea30d08d6`):

```text
→ 10 releasing changeset(s), 2 breaking (0 declared major, 2 annotated), 1 release-nothing, 2 commit(s) without a changeset
⚠️ 2 of these carry a breaking change: 2 by the author's own breaking annotation in the changeset body — …
```

The two breaking entries:

- objectui `e8fc452c3`, `.changeset/12254-envelope-draw-retire.md`: counted before and after.
- objectui `10aba37d1`, `.changeset/12242-types-field-metadata-family.md`: now counted, and its line now reads `- **minor** — **BREAKING** — The exported field metadata types stop declaring …`.

The artifact has no other diff. PR #23110's hand-corrected console changeset, `scripts/bump-objectui.sh`, `.objectui-sha` and every `.changeset/` file are untouched.

## Self-test cases (battery `#23112`, 16)

Direct, against the criterion and the renderer:

1. objectui#12242's changeset body reads breaking: its verbatim heading `## ⚠️ BREAKING, priced as minor under the fixed group's version policy`, with a guard that the fixture really carries U+26A0 U+FE0F.
2. The plain-heading control (`## BREAKING, …`) still reads breaking.
3. Decorated **prose** containing the word does not read breaking: `⚠️ Upgrade note: nothing in this change is breaking …`, `## ⚠️ Read before upgrading — this is not breaking`, `⚠️ Non-breaking cleanup; a groundbreaking refactor.`
4. The sign **before** the emphasis mark: objectui's own wrapped `⚠️ **BREAKING (scored minor per this repository's version-alignment` label. Its emphasis run crosses a line, so only the opener can answer.
5. The sign **inside** the emphasis mark: `**⚠️ Breaking for consumers that read result.data.**`.
6. The sign opening a plain paragraph: `⚠️ Breaking in places, …`.
7. The sign without its variation selector: `## ⚠ BREAKING` (U+26A0 alone).
8. The class, not the one sign: `- 🚨 BREAKING:` behind a bullet.
9. ASCII punctuation is not decoration. A code span naming an identifier called breaking, and a quotation (`"Breaking for TypeScript readers", below, …`), both stay prose.
10. `markBreaking` keeps an author's decorated label verbatim, and still marks a decorated ordinary summary.

Through `buildDigest`, in a fixture repo of its own (so the #6099 counts stay pinned):

11. Exactly the two decorated annotations are counted (3 releasing, 2 breaking, 2 by annotation). The decorated prose is not counted.
12. The count line reads `⚠️ 2 of these carry a breaking change: 2 by the author's own breaking annotation`.
13. The heading-annotated (12242-shaped) entry gets the marker on its line.
14. A summary that opens with a decorated label (10719-shaped) renders verbatim and is never restated. The case asserts that the entry is flagged before it reads the line, because an unflagged entry renders the same text.
15. The decorated-prose entry is not marked.
16. A range whose **only** breaking entry is the decorated heading still raises the ADR-0087 disposition question. This is the card's second consequence.

## Ablation

Both legs ran from the committed `ea30d08d6`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. In each leg the anchor hit 1 → 0 and the replacement 0 → 1. After each leg the tool confirmed that the blob equals HEAD and that `git diff HEAD` is empty.

- **Leg 1:** `DECORATION` emptied, which puts both regexes back to the base shape. 12 of the 16 `#23112` cases go red. The 4 that stay green are the plain-heading control and the three negatives. No other battery moves. Self-test exit 1.
- **Leg 2:** only `OPENS_WITH_BREAKING_LABEL` reverted. Exactly the 2 renderer cases go red: 10 (`markBreaking` verbatim) and 14 (summary verbatim, never restated).

## Bounded in-place fix: `OPENS_WITH_BREAKING_LABEL`

It sits in the same file and has the same defect class (a decoration not recognised as a breaking label). The change is mechanical: the same fragment, in the same position.

It is required by this change. Once decorated annotations are flagged, `markBreaking` would prefix `**BREAKING** — ` to an author label that opens with `⚠️ **BREAKING`. That breaks the self-test's existing "never restated" contract, and the corpus measurement above shows it would happen on 2 real changesets. No other symbol in the file changed.

## Gates (at `ea30d08d6`)

- **Derived set:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, run on the actual change set, derives 30 commands, identical to the dispatch's 30. All 30 exit 0. `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` ran detached: `✓ dispatch-gates self-test (fast tier): 1833 cases pass`, exit 0.
- **Reconciliation:** `--ran` reports `30 derived, 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- **Suites of the digest's consumers:**
  - `pnpm check:objectui-bump`: `bump-objectui self-test PASSED — 20 assertions across 5 cases`.
  - `pnpm check:changeset-gate-self-tests`: check-empty-changeset 170 assertions, including the four-carrier entry-regex agreement; check-adr-0087-registration 548; check-changeset-no-major 401.
  - `pnpm check:objectui-changeset`, the digest self-test: 147 checks, `all checks passed`.
- **Lint**, a proven narrowing:
  - The population is read from `eslint.config.mjs`: the `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` object covers `scripts/*.mjs`.
  - `--format json` reports 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - No config object enables type-aware linting (`parserOptions` carries only `ecmaVersion` / `sourceType`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.
  - The full `pnpm lint` run is CI's.
- **Changeset:** none. Root `scripts/` ships in no package's `files[]`, so this PR takes `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported for the seat to triage, not fixed here.** A parenthetical `(breaking …)` inside a bold lead label is not read as an annotation: 39 blobs / 23 paths are unflagged. Example: objectui `8a55f0ccd`, `.changeset/12059-sidebar-no-reorder.md`, whose lead label reads `@object-ui/layout (breaking, declared minor per the version policy).`, bolded. It is a different shape: the word is not at the line start, so it falls outside triage's binding line-start rule and needs its own ruling.
- **No pull, left untouched.** `BREAKING_EMPHASIS_LABEL`, which is scanned anywhere in the body, does not admit a decoration inside the run when the run sits mid-paragraph (`**⚠️ BREAKING**`). The corpus has zero occurrences of that shape.
